description: How to use reader mode in Safari on Mac: turn it on or off, change the font, set it per site, and fix a missing Reader button.

intro: To use Reader mode in Safari on Mac, open an article and click the Page menu button in the Smart Search field, then choose Show Reader. To leave Reader, click the Reader button and choose Hide Reader, or press Esc.
tldr: Click the Page menu button in the Smart Search field, then choose Show Reader. The keyboard shortcut is ⇧⌘R.
Turn Reader off with the Reader button and Hide Reader, or press Esc.
The Page menu button appears only on pages that Safari can read as an article.
Set the theme, font, and zoom from the Reader button. Safari keeps your last choices.
To set Reader for one website, use Page menu > Website Settings > Use Reader when available.

blocks.text: What Reader mode does in Safari

Reader mode strips a web article down to its text. Apple describes it as a way to hide distractions when you read articles in Safari. The headline and the story stay readable. The sidebars, banners, and other clutter around the story fall away.

That matters more than it sounds. Most people do not read every word on a web page. A Nielsen Norman Group analysis from 2008 estimated that users read at most 28% of the words on an average page, and 20% is more likely. The study used data from 25 users, and it is old. Treat the number as a rough guide, not a measurement of your own habits.
Which macOS version these steps cover

These steps come from Apple’s Safari User Guide for macOS 27 Golden Gate. Apple’s macOS 26 Tahoe version of the same guide gives the same Reader steps. MacRumors reports that macOS 27 reached all compatible Macs on Monday, September 14, 2026. Apple’s What’s new page lists Safari changes such as tab grouping and Notify Me. It lists no Reader changes.

blocks.title: Labels can shift
blocks.text: These steps come from Apple’s documentation and community threads, not from a live test on macOS 27. Menu labels can differ by Safari version and tab layout. If a name differs on your Mac, match the icon and the position, then follow the closest label.
Check that the page has an article first

Reader works on pages that Safari can read as an article. Apple’s guide says the Page menu button appears only when the page has an article that Reader can show. A news story, a blog post, or a long essay usually qualifies. A home page, a search results list, or a store category page may not.

If the button is missing, open the article itself. Click through from the list to the story, then look at the Smart Search field again. Try this first, then use the troubleshooting section for the other cases.
How to turn on Reader mode in Safari on Mac

Open the article in Safari. Look at the Smart Search field at the top of the window. Click the Page menu button in that field, then choose Show Reader. The page changes into a clean text view. You can go back at any time, as described below.

Once Reader is on, the Smart Search field shows the Reader button. Use it to change the look or to leave Reader. The Esc key works too. If you prefer the keyboard, press Shift-Command-R instead of opening the menu at all.
How to turn Reader mode off

Click the Reader button in the Smart Search field, then choose Hide Reader. You can also press Esc. Either way, the normal version of the page comes back. Esc is quicker if your hands are already on the keyboard.
Turning Reader off for one article does not turn off the feature. Reader stays available on the next article that has one. Leaving Reader is a view change, not a setting change.
Change the font, size, and background

While you read, click the Reader button at the left end of the Smart Search field. Choose a background theme, a font, or a zoom level. Apple says Reader always shows the last background theme, font, and size you chose. Set them once, and the next article uses the same look.

blocks.text: Summaries on supported pages

Some pages also offer a Summarise item in the Page menu. Apple says it appears only when the website supports it. Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 is not available in all languages or regions, and usage limits may apply. If Summarise is missing, Reader still works on the page.
Keyboard shortcuts for Reader mode

Apple’s keyboard shortcuts page for Safari lists Shift-Command-R to open Reader, and Esc to close it. Those are the two shortcuts to remember. Be careful with Command-R. On Apple’s general Mac shortcut page, Command-R reloads the page in Safari. Reader needs the Shift key, so add it on purpose.
Make Reader open automatically on one website

Reader is set per website. Open the article, click the Page menu button, and choose Website Settings. Turn on Use Reader when available. Apple describes this as a way to view webpage articles without distractions. Apple’s guide does not say how this setting relates to the global option described below, so test it on one site first.
Turn off automatic Reader on every site

Some Mac users report that Reader opens on every page. One Apple Community thread, posted in July 2025, describes a Mac on macOS 13.5 with this problem. The accepted answer says to open Safari > Settings > Websites, find When Visiting Other Websites, and switch it to Off. The original poster confirmed that it worked on their Mac.

blocks.title: Not confirmed for macOS 27
blocks.text: Apple’s documents do not confirm this path for macOS 27. Apple’s per-website guide does not say whether this pop-up controls Reader. Check the change on one article before you rely on it.
Common problems with Reader mode

Most problems trace back to one of three things. The page has no article, a per-site or global setting is in the way, or the menu names differ on your version of Safari. The troubleshooting list below covers each case. Work through it in order.
A worked example: reading a long article

Take the average page from the Nielsen Norman Group study. Its analysis used a page view of 593 words. At 20%, a reader gets through about 119 words. That is a small slice of the page, and it shows why clutter matters. The study is from 2008, so use it as context, not as a benchmark.

Here is a routine that works for long reads. Turn Reader on from the Page menu. Set the font and zoom once from the Reader button. Read from the top. Press Esc when you need the normal page back for a link or a form.
Mistakes people make

items: Looking for Reader in System Settings. The controls live in Safari, in the Smart Search field and the Page menu.
Expecting the button on every page. It shows only when Safari finds an article to display.
Pressing Command-R for Reader. Command-R reloads the page. Use Shift-Command-R instead.
Changing the font on one article and forgetting it carries over. Apple says Reader keeps your last choice for the next article.
Turning Reader off for every site when you only needed one. Start with the per-site setting.

blocks.text: When Reader is the wrong tool

Reader is built for reading. If a page depends on forms, buttons, maps, or video, the text view may hide the parts you need. Switch back with Hide Reader or Esc, then use the normal page to finish the task.
Reader also suits articles you plan to read, not pages you plan to scan for prices or options. A product grid, for example, has no article for Reader to show, so the button may not appear.
Quick checklist

items: Open the article, not the home page or a list.
Press Shift-Command-R, or click the Page menu button and choose Show Reader.
Adjust the theme, font, or zoom from the Reader button.
Press Esc, or choose Hide Reader, to return to the normal page.

blocks.text: Next steps after you learn Reader

Once Reader feels normal, you may want to tidy the rest of Safari. [How to customize the toolbar in Safari on Mac](/how-to/customize-the-toolbar-in-safari) covers moving and removing buttons. If pop-ups get in the way of reading, [how to block pop-ups in Safari on Mac](/how-to/block-pop-ups-in-safari) explains the per-site and all-website settings.

faq.question: Is there a web version of Reader mode?
faq.answer: Apple’s documentation describes Reader as part of Safari on Mac. It does not describe a separate web version, so this page covers Safari only.

faq.question: Why does the Reader button appear on some pages but not others?
faq.answer: Reader needs a page with an article it can show. Apple’s guide says the Page menu button appears only when that is true. Try the article’s own page instead of a list, index, or home page.

faq.question: What is the shortcut for Reader mode in Safari?
faq.answer: Shift-Command-R opens Reader, and Esc closes it. Apple lists both on its Safari keyboard shortcuts page. Command-R reloads the page, so keep the Shift key in the combination.

faq.question: Can I make Reader mode the default in Safari?
faq.answer: Apple describes a per-website setting called Use Reader when available. For a global change, a community answer says to set When Visiting Other Websites to Off. Apple does not confirm that path for macOS 27, so test it first.

faq.question: Does Reader mode need Apple Intelligence?
faq.answer: Reader itself sits in the Page menu. The Summarise item depends on the website and on Apple Intelligence, which is not available in all languages or regions. Usage limits may apply.

faq.question: Which macOS versions have these steps?
faq.answer: These steps match Apple’s Safari User Guide for macOS 27 Golden Gate. Apple’s macOS 26 Tahoe version gives the same Reader steps. MacRumors reports that macOS 27 reached compatible Macs on September 14, 2026.

faq.question: Does Reader mode work on iPhone?
faq.answer: This page covers Safari on Mac only. A community thread describes an iPhone path, but it was not checked against Apple’s iOS guide. Check Apple’s iPhone documentation before you rely on it.

faq.question: Why does my font change go back to the old setting?
faq.answer: It usually does not. Apple says Reader always shows the last background theme, font, and size you chose. If the look changed, open the Reader button at the left end of the Smart Search field and set it again.

steps.name: Open an article in Safari
steps.text: Go to a page with a long article, such as a news story or a blog post. Reader needs an article to work with, so skip the home page and the search results.

steps.name: Find the Page menu button
steps.text: Look at the Smart Search field at the top of the Safari window. Click the Page menu button in that field. Apple’s guide uses this name for the button.
steps.tip: If the Page menu button is missing, the page has no article that Safari can detect.

steps.name: Choose Show Reader
steps.text: From the Page menu, choose Show Reader. The page changes into a clean text view with the article in the centre.
steps.tip: Shift-Command-R does the same thing from the keyboard. Command-R alone reloads the page.

steps.name: Adjust the look
steps.text: Click the Reader button at the left end of the Smart Search field. Pick a background theme, a font, or a zoom level. Safari keeps your last choices for the next article.
steps.tip: Change the look once, then read a few articles to check it suits you.

steps.name: Turn Reader off
steps.text: Click the Reader button in the Smart Search field, then choose Hide Reader. You can also press Esc. The normal version of the page comes back.

steps.name: Set Reader for one website
steps.text: Open the article, click the Page menu button, and choose Website Settings. Turn on Use Reader when available. Apple describes this as a per-site setting, so other sites keep their own behaviour.
steps.tip: Test the setting on one site before you change anything else.

steps.name: Stop Reader opening on every site
steps.text: If Reader opens on every page, a community answer says to open Safari > Settings > Websites. Find When Visiting Other Websites and switch it to Off. Apple does not confirm this path for macOS 27, so check the result on your Mac.
steps.tip: Reload an article after you change the setting to see whether it took effect.

troubleshooting.problem: The Page menu button is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Safari shows the button only when the page has an article it can read. Open a full article, not a home page, a search results list, or a dashboard. If it still does not appear, the page has no article Safari can detect.

Check the per-site setting under Page menu > Website Settings first. For a global change, follow the community steps in Safari > Settings > Websites. That answer comes from a macOS 13.5 report, not from Apple’s macOS 27 documentation.

troubleshooting.problem: I cannot find Reader in System Settings
troubleshooting.fix: Reader is controlled in Safari, not in System Settings. Use the Smart Search field and the Page menu. One Apple Community user on macOS Sonoma had the same search problem, and no fix was posted.

troubleshooting.problem: Reader disappeared after a Safari update
troubleshooting.fix: A macOS 12.6 user reported this in Apple Community, and no answer was posted. Confirm the page still has an article, install the latest macOS updates, then reload the page. If the button stays missing, contact Apple Support.

troubleshooting.problem: My menu names do not match these steps
troubleshooting.fix: Apple’s older pages and forum posts describe Reader in different places, and labels shift between Safari versions. Look for the Page menu button and the Reader button in the Smart Search field. If they still differ, check Apple’s Safari User Guide for your macOS version.
